papers.title: Phylogenomics, spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and Cis-regulatory architecture underlying the Portulaca oleracea antioxidant network under extreme salinity.
papers.abstract: Global soil salinization severely threatens agricultural productivity. Portulaca oleracea L., an extreme xerohalophyte, displays exceptional salinity tolerance, yet the transcriptional architecture coordinating its antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages remains unresolved. In this study, multi-tissue high-throughput RNA-Seq, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) validation, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network (GRN) modeling were integrated to characterize 436 antioxidant loci in P. oleracea. Under chronic hypers
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-tissue RNA-Seq, qRT-PCR, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network modeling to characterize 436 antioxidant loci in the extreme halophyte Portulaca oleracea under chronic hypersalinity. It reveals spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and cis-regulatory architecture coordinating antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages, providing a resource for understanding salinity tolerance mechanisms.

papers.title: Amino Acid Metabolic Signature Links Pediatric Environmental Enteric Dysfunction to Maternal-Fetal Growth Restriction Across Two Independent Cohorts.
papers.abstract: Environmental Enteric Dysfunction (EED) is a leading contributor to childhood stunting. Most EED literature derives from postnatal pediatric cohorts, leaving unclear how much of the metabolic signature reflects acquired intestinal pathology versus growth restriction originating earlier. We applied genome-scale metabolic modeling to explore whether metabolic features of pediatric EED overlap with those of maternal plasma proteomes associated with adverse early-life growth. Duodenal transcriptomics from the Study of Environmental Enteropathy and Malnutrition (SEEM; 52 children with EED, 24 contr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used genome-scale metabolic modeling to compare duodenal transcriptomic profiles from children with environmental enteric dysfunction (EED) against maternal plasma proteomic signatures linked to adverse fetal growth. The authors found overlapping amino acid metabolic signatures across two independent cohorts, suggesting that some of the metabolic features of pediatric EED may reflect growth restriction that originates in utero rather than being purely acquired intestinal pathology.

papers.title: Nutrient control enables metabolic reconstruction of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG and analysis of secretions.
papers.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) is an important gut commensal bacterial strain that has been extensively studied in both industrial and health settings. Despite its long history of study, a high-quality genome-scale metabolic network model (GEM) for LGG has yet to be reconstructed. Only automatically generated draft models have been published, which have notoriously limited functional accuracy. Furthermore, comprehensive nutrient requirements have not been established for well-controlled in vitro studies. Here, we present the first curated GEM for LGG using a new approach for reconstruct
papers.summary: The authors present the first manually curated genome-scale metabolic model for the probiotic gut bacterium Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG, built using a new reconstruction approach that incorporates experimentally determined nutrient requirements. They also establish defined nutrient conditions for controlled in vitro growth studies and use the model to analyze secretion products. This provides a more accurate computational framework for studying LGG metabolism than previously available draft models.

papers.title: Stochasticity in Metabolism: Oxidative Stress Response Phenotypes As Emergent Consequences of Network Topology.
papers.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are ubiquitous yet elusive due to their reactivity and short half-lives, making simulation essential for mechanistic insight. Traditional ROS modeling has been confined to small ODE frameworks limited by kinetic-parameter scarcity. Here, we recast ROS dynamics as a flux-balance analysis (FBA) optimization problem using COBRA and CPLEX, augmenting the Escherichia coli iJO1366 genome-scale model with 84 spontaneous oxidation, 14 redox, and 9 detoxification reactions, targeting three ROS species: hydroxyl radicals (•OH), superoxide (•O 2 -), and hydrogen peroxide (H
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors extend the E. coli genome-scale metabolic model iJO1366 with 107 new reactions covering spontaneous oxidation, redox, and detoxification of three reactive oxygen species, and reformulate ROS dynamics as a flux-balance analysis optimization problem. This enables genome-scale simulation of oxidative stress response without requiring scarce kinetic parameters, revealing that stress phenotypes can emerge from network topology and stochastic effects.

papers.title: Temporal multi-omics reveals regulatory transitions and renoprotective candidates in cisplatin-induced kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Cisplatin is a classic first-line platinum drug extensively used in chemotherapy for solid tumors, yet its clinical applications are limited by dose-dependent nephrotoxicity. The dynamic molecular mechanisms underlying cisplatin-induced kidney injury and regeneration remain incompletely understood. Here, we established two complementary mouse models, a single high-dose cisplatin (SHDC) model and a repeated low-dose cisplatin (RLDC) model, to recapitulate acute and progressive/persistent patterns of renal injury, respectively. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses reveal temporal tra
papers.summary: This study uses two mouse models of cisplatin-induced kidney injury (single high-dose and repeated low-dose) to profile transcriptomic and proteomic changes over time. The integrated multi-omics analysis uncovers dynamic regulatory transitions during injury and identifies candidate genes with renoprotective potential. These findings improve understanding of the molecular progression of cisplatin nephrotoxicity and suggest new targets for protective strategies.

papers.title: Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) govern many cell processes. While multistability and oscillations are common GRN dynamics, they are typically studied and engineered in isolation. Here, we challenge this separation using the AC-DC circuit, a minimal three-gene network that merges the classical toggle switch and repressilator. Using a thermodynamic formalism and Bayesian inference, we show that a single-inducer version of the circuit displays diverse multifunctional dynamics, including coexistence of oscillations and multistability. We explore robustness, classify emergent behaviors, and analyze
papers.summary: This study analyzes the AC-DC genetic circuit, a three-gene network combining a toggle switch and a repressilator, and shows that a single-inducer version can exhibit multiple dynamical behaviors simultaneously, including coexisting oscillations and multistability. Using thermodynamic modeling and Bayesian inference, the authors map out a 'dynamical zoo' of behaviors and assess their robustness. The work challenges the traditional separation of studying multistability and oscillations in isolation, suggesting that real gene regulatory networks may be more multifunctional than previously appreciated.

papers.title: Robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication modulates cell fate decisions by relaying information across tissues and inducing intracellular responses mediated by gene regulatory networks. Although the inference of cell-cell communication from high-throughput data is gaining popularity, studying how communication pathways operate across biological scales and influence cell fate decisions remains challenging. Here, we present scRICH (robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells), a computational framework that leverages single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data to unravel the he
papers.summary: The authors present scRICH, a computational framework for inferring cell-cell communication from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data while explicitly accounting for heterogeneity across cells and biological scales. The method aims to robustly identify communication pathways and link them to downstream gene regulatory effects that influence cell fate decisions.

papers.title: Revisiting Ehrlich carcinoma in the era of precision oncology: bridging classical models with modern systems biology.
papers.abstract: Ehrlich carcinoma (EC) and its ascitic form, Ehrlich ascites carcinoma (EAC), are among the oldest and most widely used experimental tumor models in cancer research. Although they have traditionally been used for anticancer drug screening, their potential to address broader aspects of aggressive tumor biology has received comparatively less attention. EC/EAC exhibits several characteristics associated with advanced malignancy, including rapid tumor growth, angiogenesis, immune dysregulation, metabolic changes, therapeutic resistance, and complex interactions between the tumor and host. These f
papers.summary: This review argues that Ehrlich carcinoma and its ascitic form, long used mainly for anticancer drug screening, are underappreciated models for studying aggressive tumor biology. The authors highlight how these tumors capture features of advanced malignancy—rapid growth, angiogenesis, immune dysregulation, metabolic reprogramming, and therapy resistance—and propose integrating them with modern systems biology approaches in precision oncology.

papers.title: Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. Models contextualized with transcriptomic data from cultures at 37°C p
papers.summary: Using transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors show that pathogenic Leptospira cultured at host-like 37°C upregulates glucose uptake and metabolism, contrary to the long-held view that this bacterium relies mainly on fatty acids and has limited glucose use. Temperature therefore acts as a key cue reshaping metabolic capacity during host infection.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
papers.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.
papers.summary: The authors present MNRS, a computational framework that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from patients with six immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to identify drug combinations that could overcome primary non-response to targeted therapies. By analyzing how individual drugs reverse disease-associated expression signatures over time, the method prioritizes promising drug pairs from a vast combinatorial space. This offers a systems-biology strategy for rational combination therapy selection in IMIDs.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: The authors present a computational framework that combines machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how microbiome composition affects tumor metabolism and drug response in colorectal cancer. The model was trained on 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and can predict synergistic drug combinations in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum and other microbes. This provides a new approach for designing microbiome-aware combination therapies.

papers.title: Donor-Resolved Analysis of HES1-Associated Fibroblast States in Systemic Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc) and the rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat. Methods: We analysed 325,636 skin cells from 230 donors across five non-redundant cohorts using complete computational transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data and spatial assays. Donors or independent simulations were the inference units, with cohort adjustment and multiplicity correction where applicable. Three independent 200 ns molecular dynamics runs per condition c
papers.summary: This study analyzed over 325,000 skin cells from 230 donors across five cohorts to characterize HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc), using transcription-factor screens, donor-level trajectory analysis, multiome data, and spatial assays. The authors present this as a rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat in SSc, supported by molecular dynamics simulations. The work emphasizes donor-resolved inference rather than pooling cells, aiming to identify robust fibroblast state signatures.

papers.title: Metabolic modeling with reverse mapping links host perturbations to Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Understanding host-pathogen interactions during Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection has largely relied on identifying bacterial genes essential for intracellular survival. However, conventional reverse genetics approaches often overlook host pathways that regulate Mtb growth. Here, we developed a backtracing strategy to link host metabolic modulators with specific Mtb proteins. A genome-scale host metabolic model integrated with lung transcriptomic data from H37Rv-infected mice predicted 18 host proteins essential for Mtb survival. We validated this through pharmacological inhibition, s
papers.summary: The authors developed a backtracing strategy that integrates a genome-scale host metabolic model with lung transcriptomic data from Mtb-infected mice to identify host proteins whose metabolic activity supports bacterial survival. They predicted 18 such host proteins and validated them through pharmacological inhibition, linking host metabolic perturbations to specific Mtb proteins. This approach complements traditional bacterial reverse genetics by revealing host pathways that regulate Mtb growth.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis reveals autophagy-associated transcriptional vulnerability of dopaminergic neurons after atrazine exposure.
papers.abstract: Atrazine (ATZ) is a widely used triazine herbicide with potential neurotoxic effects, but the cell-type-specific responses of midbrain dopaminergic neurons to ATZ exposure remain poorly defined. In this study, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing to midbrain tissues from adult male mice exposed to ATZ for 28 days (a sub-acute exposure) to characterize transcriptional alterations associated with dopaminergic neuronal injury. Three mice per group were used for scRNA-seq, and group comparisons were performed using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test, or the Kruskal-Wallis test with D
papers.summary: This study used single-cell RNA sequencing of mouse midbrain to characterize how sub-acute atrazine exposure alters dopaminergic neurons. The authors identify autophagy-associated transcriptional changes that may make these neurons vulnerable to herbicide-induced injury. The work provides cell-type-specific insight into atrazine neurotoxicity.

papers.title: Integrative analysis of Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian regulators for prioritization of drug repurposing candidates.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by complex molecular mechanisms. Growing evidence indicates that circadian rhythm disruption contributes to disease progression and interacts with pathogenic pathways. Although multi-omics resources, compound perturbation profiles, and pharmacological bioactivity data are increasingly available, their integrative use for drug repurposing prioritization in AD, particularly with explicit consideration of circadian rhythm, remains limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to prioritize drug repurposing candida
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian rhythm regulators and compound perturbation/pharmacological data to prioritize drug repurposing candidates. By explicitly incorporating circadian biology into network-based analysis, it identifies compounds that may target both AD pathogenic pathways and circadian disruption. The work demonstrates a framework for combining diverse data resources to nominate repurposing candidates for a complex neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: MetworkPy: A Python Package for Graph- and Information-theoretic Investigation of Metabolic Networks.
papers.abstract: Metabolism plays an important role in physiology and disease. In silico Genome-Scale Metabolic Models (GSMMs) are useful for informing analysis of metabolism and contextualizing high-throughput molecular profiling data. Flux balance analysis (FBA) based approaches can use GSMMs to predict metabolic reaction flux states and condition-specific alterations, but most FBA methods are limited by: 1) needing metabolic objective functions that are difficult to define experimentally, and 2) confining comparisons to extrema of reaction flux distributions.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MetworkPy is a new Python package that analyzes genome-scale metabolic models using graph theory and information theory instead of traditional flux balance analysis. This approach avoids the need for experimentally difficult objective functions and allows comparison of full flux distributions rather than just their extremes, making it easier to contextualize high-throughput molecular profiling data.

papers.title: scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference from single-cell transcriptomes is complicated by expression patterns associated with both cell state and shared ancestry. Cellular phylogenies provide developmental context, but incorporating relationships among individual cells into gene-level regulatory inference remains challenging.
papers.summary: scPhyloGRN is a new computational method that infers gene regulatory networks from single-cell developmental transcriptomes by explicitly incorporating the lineage tree (phylogeny) relating individual cells. By using lineage topology to distinguish expression variation due to shared ancestry from that due to cell state, it aims to produce more accurate gene-level regulatory inferences than methods that ignore developmental relationships.

papers.title: Engineering rhizosphere microbial consortia for soil bioremediation: Mechanisms, field constraints, and evidence-based design.
papers.abstract: Soil contamination continues to threaten ecosystem health and agricultural productivity worldwide. However, rhizosphere-mediated bioremediation has emerged as a nature-inspired, sustainable approach for mitigating these impacts. This review advocates field-scale implementation of rhizosphere microbiome engineering by exploiting interactions among plants, microorganisms, and soil. Unlike previous reviews that primarily summarize rhizosphere-mediated remediation processes, it integrates mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives to identify critical barriers limiting field performance
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This review argues for moving rhizosphere microbiome engineering from lab to field for soil bioremediation, integrating mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives on plant-microbe-soil interactions. It identifies key barriers that limit field performance and proposes evidence-based design principles for engineering microbial consortia. The work is a synthesis rather than new data, aimed at guiding practical field-scale implementation.

papers.title: A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.
papers.abstract: Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is the most prevalent sensory deficit in older adults, yet its molecular progression remains poorly resolved. Few cochlear single-cell studies have integrated cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction, and cross-cohort bulk validation into one temporal framework.
papers.summary: This study builds a time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of the aging mouse cochlea, tracking how different cell types change across the lifespan. It reports two phases of age-related inflammation (biphasic inflammaging) and identifies Tbx2 as a transcription factor required for maintaining inner hair cells. The work combines cell-cell communication analysis, gene regulatory network reconstruction, and bulk RNA-seq validation across cohorts.

papers.title: Genome-scale metabolic model analysis of Korean Campylobacter jejuni isolates reveals lineage-level metabolic structure.
papers.abstract: Genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs) of Campylobacter jejuni (C. jejuni) have been studied mainly for reference strains, and their characteristics at the lineage level remain poorly understood. We reconstructed GSMMs for 86 C. jejuni isolates collected in Korea using gapseq and analyzed them together with in vitro substrate utilization data for seven substrates measured on the same isolates. Strain-specific GSMMs clustered by clonal complex (CC): in all nine CCs with ≥ 2 isolates the mean within-CC Jaccard distance was smaller than the mean between-CC distance; across all strain pairs the med
papers.summary: The authors reconstructed genome-scale metabolic models for 86 Korean Campylobacter jejuni isolates and found that strain-specific models cluster by clonal complex, with within-lineage models more similar to each other than to models from other lineages. They validated these models against in vitro substrate utilization data for seven substrates measured on the same isolates, showing that metabolic structure is organized at the lineage level.

papers.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
papers.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul
papers.summary: This study examined how expression of the protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 relates to semen quality in rams, using 15 ejaculates from five animals. Higher protamine expression was associated with better total sperm motility, and gene regulatory network analysis was used to identify potential upstream regulators of these genes. The work extends protamine biology from well-studied species into sheep reproduction.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods so that method weighting varies from edge to edge rather than being fixed globally. They also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, this score-level meta-classifier offers a way to resolve disagreements between inference methods more principledly than picking one method or simple averaging.

papers.title: Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization severely threatens global food security, necessitating systematic investigations of halophytes like Portulaca oleracea to decode the molecular mechanisms of environmental resilience. Utilizing an integrated framework of deep learning-based genome annotation (58,817 predicted genes; 96.5% BUSCO completeness), multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, the synergistic orchestration of 78 aquaporins (AQPs), 525 heat shock proteins (HSPs), and 119 late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins was elucidated. The active transcriptome, encompassi
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study combined deep-learning-based genome annotation, multi-tissue RNA-seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network inference to characterize aquaporins, heat shock proteins, and LEA proteins in the halophyte Portulaca oleracea under salt stress. The authors produced a high-completeness genome annotation (58,817 genes, 96.5% BUSCO) and identified 78 AQPs, 525 HSPs, and 119 LEAs, revealing their coordinated transcriptional regulation. The work provides a resource for understanding salt-tolerance mechanisms in halophytes.

papers.title: Decoding the epithelial-stromal interactome in allergic rhinitis through single-cell multiomics integration.
papers.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a prevalent chronic condition, yet the cellular and molecular changes associated with its pathogenesis remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell multiomics data to map the interactions between epithelial and stromal cells in allergic rhinitis, aiming to uncover cellular and molecular drivers of disease pathogenesis. The work provides a detailed interactome that may reveal novel therapeutic targets and improve understanding of chronic inflammation in AR.

papers.title: Endothelial SLC25A13 links glutamine metabolism to angiogenesis.
papers.abstract: Attention to exploring endothelial cell (EC) metabolism is increasing, but a holistic perspective on the metabolic adaptations of ECs during angiogenic proliferation is still missing. Here, we use a previously in-house developed computational EC-adapted genome-scale metabolic model that recapitulates known metabolic features in proliferating ECs to predict novel pathways central to biomass synthesis. We unveil the metabolic function of the glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13, previously overlooked in ECs, as a key regulator of glutamine utilization and provide evidence regarding its contri
papers.summary: Using an endothelial cell-adapted genome-scale metabolic model, the authors predicted and experimentally validated that the mitochondrial glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13 is a key regulator of glutamine utilization in proliferating endothelial cells. This previously overlooked transporter supports biomass synthesis and angiogenesis, linking glutamine metabolism to new blood vessel formation.

papers.title: A metabolic model based on a pangenome core reveals putative conserved biochemical features of the phytopathogen Xylella fastidiosa.
papers.abstract: Xylella fastidiosa is a xylem-limited phytopathogenic bacterium responsible for severe diseases in many economically important crops. Despite its impact, its metabolism remains poorly characterized due to fastidious growth and the limited availability of defined culture media. Here, we reconstruct the first pangenome-based genome-scale metabolic model for X. fastidiosa, integrating conserved metabolic functions from 18 strains across five subspecies. The resulting consensus model, iXfcore, is manually curated and used to explore the species' metabolic capabilities. Model simulations predict mi
papers.summary: The authors reconstructed the first pangenome-based genome-scale metabolic model for the plant pathogen Xylella fastidiosa, integrating conserved metabolic functions across 18 strains and five subspecies. The manually curated consensus model, iXfcore, was used to predict metabolic capabilities and identify putative conserved biochemical features of the species. This provides a new computational resource for studying a fastidious pathogen that is difficult to culture.

papers.title: Hybrid genome‑scale metabolic modeling and machine learning reveal cost‑efficient strategies for phototrophic polyhydroxybutyrate production in Rhodopseudomonas palustris.
papers.abstract: Plastic pollution from fossil-based materials is a major global environmental challenge. Microbially derived bioplastics, such as polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), offer a promising biodegradable alternative. However, the high substrate and operational costs of PHB production remain a major barrier to large-scale deployment. Optimizing PHB synthesis requires navigating a multidimensional design space of metabolic, nutritional, and operational variables, which is impractical to explore experimentally. This study presents an integrated computational framework that combines a genome-scale metabolic mode
papers.summary: This study combines a genome-scale metabolic model of Rhodopseudomonas palustris with machine learning to explore the design space for phototrophic polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) production. The hybrid framework identifies cost-efficient combinations of metabolic, nutritional, and operational variables that improve PHB yields, offering a computational alternative to impractical exhaustive experimental screening. The approach provides actionable strategies for lowering bioplastic production costs.

papers.title: Causality analysis of toxicological mechanisms in networked systems such as adverse outcome pathway networks.
papers.abstract: This paper examines why robust causality assessment is central to toxicology yet increasingly difficult in networked biological systems, including Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) networks and multi-omics datasets. Classical causal frameworks (e.g., Koch/Dale reasoning and Bradford Hill-type considerations) remain useful for scoping, but they offer limited operational guidance for multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-dominated mechanisms. We therefore synthesize a modern toolbox for causality analysis in toxicology spanning directed acyclic graphs for explicit causal assumptions, quantitative
papers.summary: This review argues that traditional causality frameworks like Koch's postulates and Bradford Hill criteria are insufficient for analyzing toxicological mechanisms in complex networked systems such as Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) networks and multi-omics data. It synthesizes a modern causal inference toolbox—including directed acyclic graphs for making causal assumptions explicit and quantitative methods—to better handle multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-driven mechanisms in toxicology.

papers.title: Proteomics and network biology insights into inflammation suppression during prolonged high-altitude hypoxia acclimatization.
papers.abstract: For decades, the study of high-altitude acclimatization has been a vital area of scientific inquiry aimed at enhancing human resilience, particularly in the context of military deployments. While most existing research has focused on acute inflammatory responses to hypoxia, limited information is available on the molecular mechanisms underlying long-term high-altitude acclimatization. To address this gap, the present study investigated the plasma proteomic alterations associated with 120 days of high-altitude exposure at 14,500 ft by employing quantitative proteomics combined with computationa
papers.summary: This study used quantitative plasma proteomics combined with computational network analysis to profile molecular changes during 120 days of acclimatization at 14,500 ft. The key finding is that prolonged high-altitude hypoxia exposure is associated with suppression of inflammatory pathways, extending beyond the acute inflammatory responses typically studied. The work provides proteomic and network-level insight into long-term adaptation mechanisms relevant to human resilience at altitude.

papers.title: Neutrophil-microglia communication through the C3-C3aR1 axis contributes to secondary neuroinflammation after traumatic brain injury.
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers a rapidly evolving neuroinflammatory response that contributes to secondary brain injury. Although infiltrating leukocytes and resident microglia are both prominent components of this response, the cellular signals that connect peripheral immune-cell recruitment to microglial state remodeling remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study investigates how peripheral immune cells and resident microglia communicate after traumatic brain injury to drive secondary neuroinflammation. The authors identify the complement C3-C3aR1 signaling axis as a key mediator of neutrophil-microglia crosstalk, linking infiltrating neutrophils to changes in microglial state. This suggests the C3-C3aR1 pathway as a potential therapeutic target for limiting secondary brain injury.

papers.title: Bringing translational structure to complex immune-mediated conditions: the ACT (Activation-Constraint-Tissue Context) framework for divergent phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Immune-mediated outcomes diverge across individuals with similar genetic backgrounds and environmental exposures, reflecting trajectories through a dynamic, context-dependent, and partially stochastic state space rather than fixed molecular endpoints. Despite advances in systems immunology, computational modeling, and multi-omic profiling, translating this complexity into clinically actionable reasoning remains difficult: these disciplines generate increasingly detailed representations of immune behavior that deepen mechanistic understanding while raising barriers to integration across clinica
papers.summary: This perspective proposes the ACT (Activation-Constraint-Tissue Context) framework to explain why individuals with similar genetic and environmental backgrounds develop divergent immune-mediated phenotypes. The framework conceptualizes immune outcomes as trajectories through a dynamic, context-dependent state space defined by activation, constraint, and tissue context, aiming to make complex systems immunology data more clinically actionable. It is a conceptual contribution rather than an empirical study.

papers.title: Targeting the gut-tumor axis: probiotic therapy as an adjunct strategy in colorectal cancer treatment.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a multifactorial disease driven by interactions among host genetics, immune dysregulation, environmental factors, and gut microbiota. The gut-tumor axis regulates CRC progression through inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, epithelial barrier disruption, and immune imbalance. Probiotic-derived metabolites act as bioactive molecules capable of restoring host-microbiome homeostasis and modulating tumor-associated pathways.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This review examines how the gut-tumor axis influences colorectal cancer progression through inflammation, oxidative stress, barrier disruption, and immune imbalance, and how probiotic-derived metabolites may restore host-microbiome homeostasis and modulate tumor-associated pathways. It positions probiotic therapy as a potential adjunct strategy alongside conventional CRC treatment.
